svg.title: Turn admission and governance signals
svg.desc: TurnRunner.admitTurn runs four governance steps in order: a read-only daily budget check, the session lock with the global cap, loop detection, and the global rate window. Each step can refuse the turn or emit an operator-visible signal. Only the budget check precedes the lock.

g.text: Hover a step for what it checks; its signals and refusals light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: The lock comes before steps 3 and 4 because both record state: an attempt the global cap rejects must not count.

g.text: Daily budget · checkBudget only reads: it never records, which is why it may precede the lock
The first crossing of 80 % today emits the warning; under action block a turn at 100 % or more is rejected. A storage error propagates.
Session lock · SessionLockManager.acquire waits for a same-session lock, then checks the global cap
A waiting turn emits TurnWaitStateChangedEvent at 30 s and stuck at 120 s. At the cap it throws BusyTurnException at once; nothing queues.
Loop chain · turn-chain depth first, then token velocity; a human message resets the chain
Both mechanisms fire LoopDetectedEvent; under action abort they throw LoopDetectedException and the lock is released.
Rate window · the global sliding window; a successful check() records the turn
While the window is full the turn sleeps 1 s and retries. Admission then passes to ExecutionCoordinator (section 7).
budget_warning · SSE budget_warning (tokens_used, budget, percentage, action) and a message to the originating channel
The warn-once marker budget_warning_posted_at is in the day's usage_daily aggregate, so it survives a restart.
TurnWaitStateChangedEvent · same-session wait: waiting, then stuck, with a can-cancel flag
Reaches the task stream as turn_wait_state and the global stream as conversation_changed with work_state.
LoopDetectedEvent · alert type loop_detected (critical) and SSE loop_detected via EventBusSseBridge
Fires in warn and abort mode alike; the configured action decides whether the turn then proceeds.
rate_limit_warning · SSE rate_limit_warning once per approach, with the usage ratio
The global limit is the only governance limit that defers a turn instead of refusing it.
BudgetExhaustedException · thrown by checkBudget under the block action at 100 % or more
A task that meets it fails non-retryable. Under the warn action the turn proceeds instead.
BusyTurnException · thrown by acquire when the global concurrency limit is reached
Callers wait on whenCapacityAvailable and re-attempt; a queued task stays queued. Never answered with a timer retry.
LoopDetectedException · thrown by checkLoopPreTurn when the action is abort
The session lock is released before the exception propagates; a task fails non-retryable.
never refuses · awaitRateLimitWindow has no refusal path
It polls until the window has room, so a burst of turns is delayed, not dropped.
recordToolCall per tool call feeds fingerprint detection; recordTokensAndCheckVelocity runs after each turn.
Velocity fires LoopDetectedEvent even in abort mode: the tokens are already spent, so the next pre-turn check aborts.
After admission, inside the turn · TurnGuardEvaluator calls recordToolCall; TurnRunner calls recordTokensAndCheckVelocity
